Sahil Singh vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:28811) on 15 July,
2024
Author: Vinit Kumar Mathur Bench: Vinit Kumar Mathur [2024:RJ-JD:28811]
 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Civil Writ Petition No. 19010/2022 1. Sahil Singh S/o Shri Amar Singh, Aged About 24 Years,
 By Caste Rajput Resident Of Ward No. 8 Chak 5 SSW  Jhamber Tehsil And District Hanumangarh (Raj).
2. Rameshwar Meena S/o Shri Sher Singh Meena, Aged  About 27 Years, By Caste Meena Resident Of Village  Ranwal District Sawai Madhopur (Raj.).
3. Vinod Kumar Meena S/o Shri Shobha Ram Meena, Aged  About 25 Years, By Caste Meena Resident Of Village  Khajuri Kalan, Post Doongargaon Tehsil Asnawar District  Jhalawar (Raj.).
4. Duda Ram Gadri S/o Shri Dev Kishan, Aged About 24  Years, By Caste Gadri Resident Of Village Bhimpura Tehsil  Shapura District Bhilwara (Raj.).
 ----Petitioners  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Secretary, Department Of  Personal, Govt. Of Rajasthan, Secretariat, Jaipur.
2. Rajasthan Public Service Commission, Ajmer, Through Its  Secretary. 
3. Food Safety And Standards Authority Of India, New Delhi  Through Its Chief Executive Officer. 
 ----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Lucky Rajpurohit for  Mr. Rajat Arora For Respondent(s) : Mr. Rajesh Punia  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VINIT KUMAR MATHUR Order 15/07/2024 1. Heard learned counsel for the parties. 
Sahil Singh vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:28811) on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14995539/
1 2. In pursuance of the directions issued by this Court on 03.07.2024, the learned counsel for the respondent-RPSC, Ajmer has produced the results of the petitioners before this Court in sealed cover. As per the results produced, except for petitioner No.3 i.e. Vinod Kumar Meena, the petitioner No.1-Sahil Singh, [2024:RJ-JD:28811] (2 of 2) [CW-19010/2022] petitioner No.2-Rameshwlar Meena and petitioner No.4-Duda Ram Gadri have failed in the examinations. 
3. The original result is returned in the sealed cover to learned counsel for the respondent-RPSC and photocopy of the same is taken on record. Accordingly, the respondents are directed to declare the withheld result of the petitioners. 
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the writ petition was filed on an anticipation that the degree held by the petitioners are not as per the eligibility conditions shown in the notification dated 21.10.2022. Learned counsel further submits that so far, the candidature of the petitioners has not been found to be ineligible as no orders adverse to the petitioners have been passed. 
5. Thus, in the opinion of this Court, the writ petition is premature as neither any order adverse to the petitioners has been passed nor the petitioners have been restrained from participating in the selection process for the post of Food Safety Officer in pursuance of the notification dated 21.10.2022.
6. The present writ petition is, therefore, dismissed with liberty to the petitioners to approach the appropriate forum for the redressal of their grievances, if any order adverse to the petitioners is passed. 
7. Stay petition as well as other pending applications, if any, shall stand disposed of. 
(VINIT KUMAR MATHUR),J 353-/Arun P/-
